headline: US strikes Iran again as gold hits $4,120 and your US holdings dipped last night — but the long-term picture remains solid.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was the biggest mover last night, slipping 2.5% to $251.38. No major company-specific news drove the drop — it looks like broader tech/risk-off pressure across the NASDAQ. The long-term GTA VI thesis is unchanged; this is noise for a buy-and-hold holder.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS fell 1.9% today to $4.61, still well below its 52-week highs. Lithium prices remain soft and sentiment around the sector is cautious. Chinese battery giant CATL's Jianxiawo mine restart has added supply-side pressure. The stock is down 31.6% from cost — a tough position, but the lithium recovery story is a long-term one.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a solid session today, up 1.9% to $16.61. AI optimism got a boost from OpenAI's GPT-5.6 release news. Still sitting 12% below cost, but the momentum today is encouraging for patient holders.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 1.4% last night to $383.34. The market is weighing a reported 3,200 Xbox job cuts against upcoming quarterly earnings — Goldman Sachs flagged whether Azure's AI growth can justify ongoing investment. Earnings report coming soon; watch that space.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 1.35% last night to $358.71, slightly more than the broader market. No single catalyst — more a case of the market rotating on AI sentiment. Alphabet is still highlighting AI-driven growth in its long-term strategy, and the position is up 16.7% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.98% today to $93.97. Emerging markets felt pressure from the IMF cutting its 2026 global growth forecast to 3% and ongoing Middle East tensions. Barely underwater on cost — long-term emerging markets exposure is worth holding through this.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was essentially flat today, nudging up 0.06% to $532.46. The ASX-listed US market ETF tracks the broader US market, which was mixed last night. Up 3.25% overall — steady as she goes.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was virtually unchanged today at $75.82, up just 1 cent. Its diversified mix of global shares meant the mixed market signals largely cancelled out. A tiny 0.59% gain overall — this one just does its job quietly.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings incoming — watch Azure numbers closely
watch_today.detail: Microsoft has announced its quarterly earnings release date. Goldman Sachs is asking whether Azure's AI cloud growth can keep justifying Microsoft's massive AI investment. Last night MSFT fell 1.4% to $383.34 and is down 13.5% from your cost. For a long-term holder, earnings will be the real test — if Azure delivers, expect a bounce. If not, the stock could stay under pressure for a while. Hold for now.

watch_today.title: TTWO dip — long-term story unchanged
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 2.5% last night to $251.38, but there's no fundamental bad news — it's broad market softness. You're still up 9.6% on this position. GTA VI hype is the long-term driver here and nothing's changed on that front. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continues, but don't panic sell
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals slipped another 1.9% today to $4.61. You're now down 31.6% on this position ($47 in the red). The CATL mine restart in China is adding supply pressure and lithium prices remain soft. The case for lithium long-term (EVs, batteries) is still intact, but this one needs patience. Selling here locks in a real loss — hold unless your conviction in the sector has changed.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX bouncing — AI tailwind is real
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF rose 1.9% today to $16.61, helped by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 release news and continued AI investment momentum. Still 12% below cost, but today's move is a positive sign. Long-term AI exposure via this ETF is exactly the kind of thing to hold through the dips.

watch_today.title: US-Iran conflict escalating — watch oil and gold
watch_today.detail: The US has launched new strikes on Iran and Trump says things could get 'much worse'. Gold hit $4,120 last night (up 1.2%) as investors sought safety. Oil slipped to $72.69 despite the conflict — markets are uncertain about supply impact. Prolonged conflict is a risk to global growth and could weigh on your emerging markets (VGE) and broader equity holdings.

watch_today.title: IMF cuts global growth to 3% — a headwind for emerging markets
watch_today.detail: The IMF has cut its 2026 global growth forecast to 3%, citing geopolitical risks including the Iran conflict. This puts some downward pressure on your VGE (Emerging Markets) ETF. It's not a reason to sell — it's a long-term hold — but worth knowing this is a headwind for the next 12 months.

world.summary: The biggest story globally today is the US launching fresh strikes on Iran, with Trump warning things could get 'much worse'. The IMF has cut its global growth forecast citing geopolitical risks, and the Trump administration is ramping up pressure on US states over election laws.

stories.title: US launches new strikes on Iran — Trump warns it could get 'much worse'
stories.why_it_matters: The United States has launched a new wave of strikes against Iran overnight, with President Trump stating the attacks could get 'much worse' if Iran doesn't comply. Reuters reports Trump actually wants to leave the Iran conflict behind him, but the situation is spiralling beyond easy resolution. The Jerusalem Post says the US is now preparing for a prolonged conflict. For everyday Australians, this matters because sustained Middle East instability drives up oil prices, spooks global markets, and could hit the cost of living through petrol prices and imported goods.

stories.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast to 3%, warns Middle East conflict a major risk
stories.why_it_matters: The International Monetary Fund has downgraded its forecast for world economic growth in 2026 to just 3%, down from earlier projections, with Middle East conflict and ongoing geopolitical tensions cited as key risks. A rebound is expected in 2027, but the near-term picture is weaker. The IMF separately upgraded the UK's outlook slightly as fears about the Iran war's immediate economic impact eased. For investors, slower global growth means more pressure on corporate earnings and emerging markets — your VGE ETF is exposed to this.

stories.title: Trump administration threatens to arrest election officials over migrant voting
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has escalated its fight with US states over election laws, threatening criminal prosecution of state election officials in Oregon and elsewhere if non-citizens are found to have voted. The administration is also tying terrorism-related federal grants to states making specific election practice changes — essentially using federal funding as leverage. The NYT reports new rules requiring election changes before states can access anti-terrorism grants. This is a significant escalation in the federal vs. state standoff over election integrity rules in the US.

stories.title: Gold surges to $4,120 as investors seek safe haven amid global uncertainty
stories.why_it_matters: Gold jumped 1.2% last night to $4,120 USD per ounce — a significant move that reflects investor anxiety about the Iran conflict, slowing global growth, and geopolitical tension. When gold rises sharply, it usually means big money is moving away from riskier assets like shares and into perceived 'safe' stores of value. The Aussie dollar also nudged up slightly to 69.38 US cents, which slightly offsets the impact of US share falls for Australian investors.

stories.title: Crude oil falls to $72.69 despite Iran strikes — markets confused about supply impact
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the US launching fresh strikes on Iran — one of the world's significant oil producers — crude oil (WTI) actually fell 1.1% to $72.69 per barrel last night. This is counterintuitive but reflects market uncertainty: traders are unsure whether the conflict will directly disrupt Iranian oil exports or whether OPEC can compensate. Lower oil prices are generally good for Australia's inflation outlook and may give the RBA (Reserve Bank) some breathing room on interest rates.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 closed down 0.26% today at 8,762. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 dipped 0.28% but the NASDAQ squeezed out a small 0.2% gain. Gold spiked strongly, the Aussie dollar edged up, and oil fell.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down slightly today — IMF growth cuts and Iran tensions weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a mild pullback as Iran fears and mixed macro data weighed.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Managed a small gain last night, helped by AI-related optimism despite broader caution.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold surged as investors sought safety amid Iran strikes and global growth concerns.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell despite Iran strikes — markets uncertain about actual supply disruption.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar nudged higher, softening the impact of US share falls for Aussie investors.

politics.summary: The RBA is flagging more interest rate pain ahead, banks are making surprise mortgage moves, the IMF has cut Australia's growth outlook, and Labor is pushing new laws on AI labelling and industrial relations.

stories.title: RBA chief economist warns of more frequent supply shocks — rate rises not off the table
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA's chief economist warned today that supply shocks — disruptions to the economy from things like pandemics, wars, and climate events — will become more frequent, making the inflation fight harder. The Australian reports that both further interest rate hikes AND a higher unemployment rate remain on the table as tools in the RBA's fight against inflation. The Courier Mail describes Australia as being stuck in a 'lose-lose bind' — raise rates and hurt borrowers, don't raise them and inflation stays sticky. Not great news for anyone with a mortgage.

stories.title: Banks make surprise move on mortgage rates
stories.why_it_matters: Australian banks have made an unexpected move on mortgage rates — the details of whether this is a cut or increase aren't fully available from the article, but given the RBA backdrop and banks' cost pressures, it's worth following up if you have a variable mortgage. Any change to bank mortgage pricing outside of an official RBA decision is significant because it affects the repayments of hundreds of thousands of Australians.

stories.title: IMF downgrades Australia's economic growth forecast
stories.why_it_matters: The IMF has specifically cut its forecast for Australia's economic growth as part of its wider global downgrade. This adds to pressure on the Albanese government ahead of what's expected to be a tough second half of 2026. Slower growth means softer company earnings, more cautious consumer spending, and less tax revenue for the government. Combined with ongoing inflation concerns, it's a difficult environment for the RBA to navigate.

stories.title: Labor pushes for law requiring AI labelling in creative works
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is pushing legislation that would require AI-generated content to be clearly labelled in creative works — think music, art, writing. This comes as Australian creative industries push back against AI companies using their work to train models without payment or credit. Separately, the AFR reports AI giants' offer of a 'copyright olive branch' to creators has been rejected by both industry groups and the government, suggesting tougher regulation is coming.

stories.title: Andrew Wilkie blasts Labor's gambling laws as 'useless' — losses top $104bn since Murphy review
stories.why_it_matters: Independent MP Andrew Wilkie has labelled the Albanese government's gambling reform legislation 'useless', pointing out that Australians have lost more than $104 billion in gambling since the Murphy Review was handed down. Wilkie has long been a champion of stricter gambling laws, including online betting restrictions. The criticism suggests the government's reforms haven't gone nearly far enough to address problem gambling, which remains one of Australia's most significant social issues.

ai.summary: OpenAI dropped its latest model GPT-5.6 today, Labor is pushing AI labelling laws in Australia, and global AI regulation debates are heating up across multiple jurisdictions.

stories.title: OpenAI publicly releases GPT-5.6 — a new conversational AI model
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has announced it will publicly release GPT-5.6, a new conversational AI model. CNBC reports it's specifically designed to be better at natural, flowing conversations — think less robotic back-and-forth and more like talking with a knowledgeable person. This matters because it directly competes with Google's Gemini (relevant to your GOOG holding) and Microsoft's Copilot (MSFT). It's also arriving at the same time as Elon Musk's latest Grok release, meaning the AI model race is intensifying fast.

stories.title: OpenAI's advanced AI collides with Elon Musk's latest Grok release
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI's most capable AI model is being positioned more openly in the market at exactly the same time Elon Musk's xAI released a new version of Grok. The AI arms race is moving faster than ever, with multiple frontier models (top-tier AI systems pushing the boundaries of capability) now competing directly for users, developers, and enterprise customers. This ongoing competition is the core reason companies like Alphabet and Microsoft are spending billions on AI — and why your GXAI ETF exists.

stories.title: Labor to introduce laws requiring AI labelling in creative works
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian government is drafting laws that would force anyone publishing AI-generated creative content — music, art, writing, film — to clearly disclose it was made by AI. This is designed to protect Australian artists and creators from being displaced without acknowledgement. It follows the rejection of a copyright compromise offered by big AI companies, suggesting Australia is moving toward harder regulation of AI-generated content rather than self-regulation.

stories.title: Education unions call for human-centred AI with teacher-student relationship protected
stories.why_it_matters: Global education unions have issued a joint demand for AI in schools to be designed around protecting the teacher-student relationship rather than replacing it. The call is for 'human-centred AI' — meaning AI tools that assist teachers rather than automate their role. This is a growing tension worldwide as schools rush to adopt AI tools like ChatGPT for tutoring, marking, and lesson planning, raising real questions about the future of teaching as a profession.

sport.summary: NRL Round 19 kicks off Friday night. Wimbledon is heating up with Djokovic vs Sinner in the semis, Cruz Hewitt making waves, and Aussies in the mixed doubles final. AFL has a big Friday night blockbuster under Perth lights.

stories.title: Djokovic vs Sinner: Wimbledon semi-final blockbuster set
stories.why_it_matters: Wimbledon's men's semi-finals are set, with world No.1 Jannik Sinner renewing his rivalry with Novak Djokovic in what promises to be one of the matches of the year. Djokovic, chasing a record-extending Grand Slam title, faces the in-form Italian who has dominated the tour in 2026. This is the marquee match of Wimbledon fortnight — a genuine clash of generations.

stories.title: Cruz Hewitt fires Wimbledon statement — 'unfinished business'
stories.why_it_matters: Cruz Hewitt, son of Australian legend Lleyton Hewitt, has made a serious statement at Wimbledon 2026, advancing with a dominant performance. Fox Sports reports the 20-year-old declared he has 'unfinished business' at the All England Club. The younger Hewitt is generating serious buzz as the next Australian tennis hope, carrying on the family name at the sport's most prestigious venue.

stories.title: Aussie doubles pair reaches Wimbledon mixed doubles final
stories.why_it_matters: An Australian doubles pair has reached the mixed doubles final at Wimbledon 2026, continuing a strong tournament for Aussie tennis. The result means Australian fans have plenty to cheer for at SW19 this week, with Cruz Hewitt still in the draw and now a doubles final to look forward to.

stories.title: AFL blockbuster: The competition's top two teams face off under Perth lights tonight
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's two best teams are squaring off tonight in Perth in what's being described as a titanic battle. The Hawks are fielding a remarkable seventh debutant, while GWS are managing a key injury and the Bulldogs have a doubt over an important player for their own fixture. This is the marquee AFL match of Round 17 and a genuine finals preview.

stories.title: NRL Round 19: Full team lists confirmed — Tigers v Warriors opens the round Friday night
stories.why_it_matters: All Round 19 team lists are confirmed ahead of the round opener — Wests Tigers host the Warriors at Campbelltown on Friday night at 8pm. Jahream Bula features in the Tigers' previews and is apparently full of self-belief heading into the match. Broncos, Dragons, and Panthers are all on the bye this round. The full draw runs across the weekend with Storm vs Titans (your Gold Coast side) the Sunday night game at AAMI Park.
